title: Erdős Problem 654: the Aletheia counterexample
abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib proof that Erdős Problem 654 has a negative answer: for every m ≥ 10 there is a set of n = 4m points in the Euclidean plane, no four on a circle, in which every point has fewer than 3n/4 distinct distances to the other points. Consequently it is false that every n-point planar set with no four concyclic points has a point with (1 - o(1))n distinct distances. The construction (Aletheia; Feng et al., arXiv:2601.22401) places the points (0, ±3^(k+1)) and (±2^(j+1), 0) on the two coordinate axes.
